name: Running Start
org: Washington State Board for Community and Technical Colleges
what_you_do: 11th and 12th graders take college classes at a Washington community or technical college. They earn high school and college credit.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors in Washington. The SBCTC page does not list other requirements; contact the college's Running Start coordinator.
pay_detail: No tuition. Students and families pay mandatory fees, books and transportation.
deadline_text: Deadlines are not stated on the SBCTC page; they vary by college.
how_to_apply: Contact the Running Start coordinator at the college you want to attend (the SBCTC page links a coordinator list) and your high school counselor.
notes: Work hours tie-in from Washington L&I: 16 and 17 year olds enrolled in a bona fide college program, such as Running Start, may work non-school week hours during the regular school year (employers should ask for proof such as a college transcript).
